comments.text: を始め is used to preface a list of items, and also to emphasize the first one. A をはじめ、B, C ... English equivalents might be not only, but also Not only A, but also B and C Especially A, but also B and C similar to [karashite] which is mostly used for negative things. かれの下品の言い方からして、すごく嫌な人です I really dislike him, especially because of his foul mouth.
comments.html:
<b>を始め</b> is used to preface a list of items, and also to emphasize the first one.

A をはじめ、B, C ...

English equivalents might be <b>not only, but also</b>
Not only A, but also B and C
Especially A, but also B and C

similar to [karashite] which is mostly used for negative things.

かれの下品の言い方<b>からして</b>、すごく嫌な人です
I really dislike him, <b>especially</b> because of his foul mouth.

comments.text: used when giving a list of things, the first example being X

comments.text: を始め does not necessairly mean "to start with" but the means of enumeration. 彼は英語を始め、フランス語とロシア語にも堪能だ only serves as the means of enumeration. "He is conversant not only in English but also in French and Russian."
comments.html: を始め does not necessairly mean "to start with" but the means of enumeration. 彼は英語を始め、フランス語とロシア語にも堪能だ only serves as the means of enumeration. "He is conversant not only in English but also in French and Russian."

comments.text:
but it might also mean especially, as in this example:

田中先生をはじめ、この学校の皆さんのお世話になりました。
（たなかせんせいをはじめ、このがっこうのみなさんのおせわになりました。）
I Have been helped by everyone in this school, but especially by Mr. Tanaka.
